sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the III Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT XII, Vijaypur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.1036/2016 dated 29.12.2018.
2. Though this appeal is listed for Orders, with the consent of learned Advocates appearing for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are that:
On 22-10-2015 at about 19-30 hours, when the petitioner was proceeding on the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-28/EF-2041 going towards Indi to Hirerugi, the petitioner was riding the said motorcycle in slow and cautious manner by the extreme left side of the road, when he came near Shanti Nagar at Indi on Indi to Hirerugi road, at that time one Piaggio Auto bearing Reg. No.KA-28/A-1497 came from opposite side in a high speed, rash and negligent manner, the driver being unable to control over the same, dashed to the motorcycle of the petitioner and caused the accident.

Due to this impact, the petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and Shreekanth vs Manjula And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50980347/
2 sustained fractural injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Dr. Tanga Hospital,
Vijayapur and admitted as indoor patient for 15 days and undergone operations to his fractural injuries and implants were inserted, for which the petitioner has spend more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses.

Till today the petitioner is under follow up treatment as per advice of the Doctor and said Doctor advised the petitioner to undergo another major surgery in future for removal of implants and the cost of the surgery comes to Rs.50,000/- so the petitioner is in need of Rs.50,000/- for future medical treatment.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.4,33,600/-.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
9. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.
11. It is seen that the owner/insurer had not challenged the judgment and award and therefore accepted the liability to pay the compensation.
12. The Tribunal has assessed the disability of the petitioner to the extent of 18% only.

However, a perusal of Ex.P-4 wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries like 1/3rd tibia and fibula without DNVD, open comminuted fracture base of 4th, 5th metacarpal, burst fracture right orbit and CLW over upper lib.
Considering the nature of injuries and taking into consideration Ex.P-4 - wound certificate, this Court assess the disability at 20% instead of 18% to the whole body.
13. Insofar as claim for compensation is concerned, injuries show that claimant had suffered permanent disability.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence with regard to his income.
Therefore, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Shreekanth vs Manjula And Anr on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50980347/
3 14.
Since the accident has taken place in the year 2015, the notional income has to be taken at Rs.8,000/- p.m.
The claimant is aged about 20 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,45,600/-
(Rs.8,000/- x 12 x 18 x 20%) on account of 'loss of future income'.

15. Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment and medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that claimant is entitled for following sums in terms of memo of calculation filed by the learned counsel for the appellant:
 Awarded by Enhanced  Sl.
 Heads the Tribunal in by this  No  Rs. Court in Rs.
 Towards pain and  1 20,000/- 40,000/-
 suffering  2 Medical expenses 91,500/- 91,500/-
 Loss of future  3 2,72,160/- 3,45,600/-
 earning  Food and
nourishment

5 Attendant charges 10,000/- 10,000/-
 6 Conveyance charges 10,000/- 10,000/-
 7 Loss of amenities 20,000/- 20,000/-
 Loss of earning  8 NIL 24,000/-
 during laid up period  Total 4,33,660/-
 5,51,100  Rounder off to 4,33,600/-
16.

In view of the above, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.1036/2016 dated 29.12.2018 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.4,33,600/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.5,51,100/-.

(c) The insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

4 (d) The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) Amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the jurisdictional Tribunal for disbursement to the claimants in terms of award of the Tribunal.
(f) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
